# Next Inspect UI

> Inspect any React or Next.js component in the browser and jump to its source in your IDE.

- Site: https://niu.gxuri.me/
- npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/next-inspect-ui
- GitHub: https://github.com/Gurvinder-Singh02/next-inspect-ui
- Author: Gxuri (https://gxuri.me)

## Docs

- [Overview](https://niu.gxuri.me/): Install, usage snippets, FAQ
- [Walkthrough](https://niu.gxuri.me/walkthrough): Hover, click, Option-climb, Space trees
- [How it works](https://niu.gxuri.me/how-it-works): Fiber metadata, source maps, editor open
- [Benchmarks](https://niu.gxuri.me/benchmarks): Source lookup results and component patterns
- [API Reference](https://niu.gxuri.me/api-reference): InspectUI props
- [Shortcuts](https://niu.gxuri.me/shortcuts): Keyboard and pointer controls

## Install

```bash
npm i -D next-inspect-ui
```

Mount only in development. Dynamically import `InspectUI` behind a `NODE_ENV === "development"` (or Vite `import.meta.env.DEV`) check so production bundles tree-shake it away.

## Notes for agents

- No build plugin is required (no Webpack/Vite/Turbopack/Babel/SWC plugin).
- Works with React 19+ apps including Next.js and Vite; React 18 is experimental.
- Supported editors: Cursor, VS Code, VS Code Insiders, Windsurf, Zed.
- Optional `projectRoot` helps resolve relative paths; other props seed the settings panel.
